plan.reason: The commit relaxes validation so min_tokens=0 is accepted on Chat Completions (crates/protocols/src/chat.rs:302, range(min = 0)) and Completions (crates/protocols/src/completion.rs:99), leaving only the cross-field rule that min_tokens must not exceed max_tokens/max_completion_tokens (chat.rs:500-503, completion.rs:178-181). The current docs already match this exactly: src/lib/content/reference/api/openai.md:120 documents min_tokens as "Minimum tokens to generate; must not exceed `max_completion_tokens`" with no lower-bound restriction — unlike neighboring fields where the page explicitly notes "(at least 1)" (e.g., max_completion_tokens at line 91, top_k at line 118). The Completions endpoint inherits the same extension-field table via openai.md:358. The previous min=1 rejection was never documented, so the fix brings behavior in line with the existing documentation and no edit is needed.

Both changes require no doc edits. (1) The commit's sglang>=0.5.13 floor is superseded: current source (grpc_servicer/pyproject.toml:43) requires sglang>=0.5.20, and the current docs already state the correct current requirement — src/lib/content/getting-started/kv-events-cache-aware.md:16: "the extra requires SGLang 0.5.20 or newer". Writing 0.5.13 into docs would be stale. (2) The removal of the WatchLoadUpdateReq piggyback in grpc_servicer/smg_grpc_servicer/sglang/request_manager.py is a behavior-preserving internal refactor (replaced upstream by shmem load snapshots per the pyproject comment); no current docs page describes that internal forwarding path, so there is nothing to correct.

The commit is a pure release chore: it bumps version strings for the v1.7.0 release across Cargo.toml files, pyproject.toml files, the Helm chart, and the default `smg_commit`/tag examples in the release Docker workflows. It changes no gateway behavior, configuration options, APIs, defaults, or metrics. Current source verification shows the commit is already superseded (model_gateway/Cargo.toml is at version 1.11.0). The current docs do not hard-code any release version that would now be stale: searches for "1.6.0" and "v1.6" in the docs repo return no matches, and image-tag examples in high-availability.md and service-discovery.md use the placeholder pattern `{smg_version}-{engine}-{engine_version}` with unrelated illustrative versions. The version-bump release process itself is already documented in src/lib/content/contributing/development.md ("A `chore(release): bump versions for vX.Y.Z` PR bumps the versions... `make bump-version VERSION=X.Y.Z` updates the gateway and binding versions..."), so no documentation change is required.

The commit's sole user-facing effect is that Linux aarch64 PyPI wheels are built on manylinux_2_28 (requiring glibc 2.28+) while x86_64 stays on manylinux2014 (glibc 2.17+). The current workflow (.github/workflows/release-pypi.yml lines 24–48) confirms this is still in effect, and src/lib/content/getting-started/index.md lines 19–22 already document the exact matrix: "Linux x86_64 | manylinux2014 (glibc 2.17+), musllinux 1.1" and "Linux aarch64 | manylinux 2.28 (glibc 2.28+), musllinux 1.1". No doc change is required.

The commit only edits .github/workflows/release-pypi.yml (verified in current source at lines 187–201: a hermetic Python 3.13 setup step and `pip install -U twine` so CI's twine/packaging can parse Metadata 2.4 wheels during PyPI upload). It changes no gateway code, no published package contents, no flags/APIs/metrics, and no documented process: the only docs reference to release-pypi (src/lib/content/contributing/development.md, line 627) describes only when the workflow triggers, which is unchanged. This is internal CI release plumbing with no user-facing behavior to document.

The commit changes observable HTTP behavior on the PD router: non-streaming responses (including logprob-merged responses and their fallback paths) now carry Content-Type: application/json instead of axum's default application/octet-stream. The fix is present and active in current source, but no current docs page mentions the response content type for PD non-streaming responses, even though the docs document content-type semantics elsewhere. One small addition to the PD documentation is warranted.

concerns.title: docs(pd-disaggregation): note that non-streaming PD responses carry Content-Type: application/json
concerns.concern: Non-streaming responses returned by the HTTP PD router now always carry the Content-Type: application/json header (previously they defaulted to application/octet-stream, which broke OpenAI-style JSON clients); this applies to plain relayed decode bodies, logprob-merged responses, and all merge-failure fallback paths, while streaming PD responses continue to use text/event-stream.
concerns.evidence: model_gateway/src/routers/http/pd_router.rs lines 1613-1624 define non_stream_pd_json_response, which sets CONTENT_TYPE to application/json and whose doc comment states axum's (StatusCode, Bytes).into_response() defaults to application/octet-stream; process_non_streaming_response (lines 1627-1674) returns through this helper on every path (no-logprob relay at 1644, missing prefill body at 1648, parse failure at 1657, merged body at 1667, serialization failure at 1671). Streaming responses set text/event-stream separately at line 1607. Current docs pages concepts/routing/pd-disaggregation.md and getting-started/pd-disaggregation.md describe PD dispatch and responses but never mention the response Content-Type, and a docs-wide search for octet-stream returns no matches.

plan.reason: The commit only bumps the internal str0m WebRTC dependency from 0.20 to 0.21 in Cargo.toml with unchanged feature flags and no code changes; current source has since moved to str0m 0.23 (verified at Cargo.toml:73), and no current docs page references str0m or any dependency version. No user-facing behavior, configuration option, API, or default changed.

The commit adds only internal CI benchmarking infrastructure: a nightly, informational GitHub Actions workflow (.github/workflows/nightly-tau2.yml, verified in current source and explicitly "never a merge gate"; its PR trigger is now even disabled in current code) plus maintainer scripts (scripts/tau2/launch_arms.sh, scripts/tau2/run_ab.py), a scripts-local README, and unit tests/fixtures (scripts/tests/test_tau2_run_ab.py). No gateway runtime code, configuration, CLI, API, or metrics changed (nothing under crates/, model_gateway/, or bindings/). Current docs contain no coverage of nightly benchmark workflows (searches for "tau2" and "bfcl" return no docs matches), and contributing/development.md documents only PR-gating CI lanes and the benchmark-*/genai-bench jobs, so no existing passage becomes stale or contradictory. The README's note about SMG's auto model→parser mapping lacking a Qwen3.6 entry describes pre-existing behavior in crates/tool_parser, not a change made by this commit.

The commit only reschedules internal CI benchmark workflows: nightly-bfcl now runs Mon/Wed/Fri and nightly-tau2 Tue/Thu/Sat (verified in current .github/workflows/nightly-tau2.yml lines 20–31, cron "17 7 * * 2,4,6"), and the tau2 pull_request sanity trigger is commented out. These are informational, non-merge-gating benchmark A/B runs (the workflow header states "Informational/non-blocking — never a merge gate"). They affect no gateway runtime behavior, configuration, or API. The published docs never mention these workflows: searches for "BFCL" and "tau2" in docs return nothing, and the CI documentation in src/lib/content/contributing/development.md ("CI at a Glance", lines 633–646) covers only PR-gating and advisory jobs, not nightly benchmark schedules. The "nightly" references in docs concern nightly rustfmt and nightly container tags, unrelated to this change. Nothing in existing docs is contradicted and no user-facing behavior changed.

The commit modifies only internal CI workflow files (.github/workflows/nightly-bfcl.yml, .github/workflows/nightly-tau2.yml), switching the reasoning parser used by nightly Kimi-K2.6 benchmark jobs from kimi_k25 to kimi_thinking. No SMG runtime code, CLI surface, or parser behavior changed: current crates/reasoning_parser/src/factory.rs already registers both parsers unchanged (kimi_k25 with always_in_reasoning=false at lines 182-191, kimi_thinking with always_in_reasoning=true at lines 193-202) and the same detection patterns (lines 226-232). Their semantics are already documented correctly in current docs: src/lib/content/concepts/architecture/grpc-pipeline.md lines 226-227 show kimi_thinking "Starts in reasoning: Yes" vs kimi_k25 "No", and src/lib/content/getting-started/tokenization-and-parsing.md line 196 lists kimi_thinking among parsers that start in reasoning. The change is purely a benchmark-harness configuration fix with no effect on user-facing behavior.

The commit fixes the Helm chart so its history-backend router flags match the Python launcher's exact option names. The current docs still present this as an unresolved known issue in the "History backends in chart 1.11.0" warning without noting the fix, so the workaround guidance needs to be scoped to chart 1.11.0 and earlier.

concerns.title: docs(getting-started): scope Helm history-backend startup failure to chart 1.11.0 and note the fix
concerns.concern: The Helm chart's smg.routerArgs template now passes the Python launcher's exact history flag names (--postgres-pool-max, --redis-pool-max, --oracle-connect-descriptor, --oracle-username), so chart versions after 1.11.0 no longer make the router exit at startup when history.backend is postgres, redis, or oracle with a DSN; the docs warning still describes the bug as current and unconditionally recommends the router.extraArgs workaround.
concerns.evidence: deploy/helm/smg/templates/_helpers.tpl lines 252, 260, 265, 271 now emit "--postgres-pool-max", "--redis-pool-max", "--oracle-connect-descriptor", and "--oracle-username" (commit 089fd47b), which bindings/python/tests/test_helm_chart_args.py verifies are exact options of RouterArgs; deploy/helm/smg/Chart.yaml still says version 1.11.0, so the fix ships after that release. src/lib/content/getting-started/index.md lines 683-684 ("History backends in chart 1.11.0") still states the chart "passes a flag the gateway image rejects (--postgres-pool-max-size, --redis-pool-max-size, or --oracle-dsn), and the router exits at startup" and advises leaving history.backend at memory, without noting the issue is fixed in later chart versions.
